methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Design a circuit for an 8x1 memory.
Writing to the memory is accomplished by shifting-in bits.
MSB is shifted in first via input S.
Shift register consists of 8 D-type flip-flops.
Flip-flop outputs are labeled Q[0] to Q[7].
Enable input is synchronous active high.
Extend the circuit to have 3 additional inputs A, B, and C.
Extend the circuit to have an output Z.
Circuit should contain ONLY the 8-bit shift register and multiplexers.
spec_atomic_units: Output Z is derived from Q[0] through Q[7] of an 8-bit shift register.
Inputs A, B, and C act as select lines for an 8-to-1 multiplexer.
Multiplexer inputs are connected to Q[0], Q[1], Q[2], Q[3], Q[4], Q[5], Q[6], and Q[7].
Output Z is the selected Q[i] value based on the binary representation of ABC.
Combinational logic structure consists of an 8-to-1 multiplexer.
Select lines A, B, and C directly control which input is routed to Z.
Signal flow is from shift register outputs to multiplexer inputs.
clk input clocks the shift register.
enable input allows shifting when high.
Critical path for writing is from S through the flip-flops.
Critical path for reading is from Q[0]-Q[7] through the multiplexer to Z.
Setup and hold times for flip-flops must be met.
Shift operation occurs on the rising edge of clk when enable is high.
A, B, and C are address inputs.
Z reflects the selected register output after the propagation delay of the multiplexer.
